title: TREX-F: TRustability of Electronics using X-ray based Fingerprinting
problem: Counterfeit and tampered printed circuit boards (PCBs) infiltrate the electronics supply chain, posing risks to business and security.
motivation: Authenticating PCBs is essential for maintaining supply chain integrity and preventing circulation of forged electronics.
method: TREX-F uses X-ray microscopy (detailed X-ray imaging taken from specific angles) to capture the natural manufacturing defects in circuit boards—solder irregularities, uneven material deposition, and microscopic surface anomalies. It applies computer vision techniques to extract a unique fingerprint from these X-ray images: Canny edge detection and SIFT identify distinctive features and patterns, contour detection traces shapes, and PCA reduces the data to what matters most. Finally, it converts this fingerprint into authentication codes in QR and data-matrix barcode formats that can be scanned to verify the board's authenticity.
key_novelty: Circuit boards are authenticated by creating unique fingerprints from their natural manufacturing defects, captured via X-ray imaging and analyzed with computer vision.
contributions: X-ray imaging-based PCB fingerprint extraction using anomaly detection
Computer vision-based feature extraction (Canny, contour, PCA, SIFT)
QR and data-matrix code generation for quick authentication
~95% average authentication accuracy with ~0.1% false acceptance rate
limitations: Limited to three specific PCB types; generalization to other designs unclear.
